assets.content:
LAYOUT SPEC for last season's DAYDRIFT episode card, exactly as it went to the printer (flat, single record; to be reverse-engineered downstream).

Document: single card, 105 x 148 mm A6 PORTRAIT, single sided, NO bleed box present (trim = media box, 0 mm bleed), fonts embedded. This is the print file the printer returned for the 2025 (season three) run and the only copy the show still has.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED (reads as six tidy blocks):
- Top: the EPISODE NUMBER, e.g. 'Episode 7', warm humanist serif, medium.
- Under it: the EPISODE TITLE, large, warm humanist serif.
- Under that: the GUEST CREDIT line in the humanist sans, e.g. 'With Priya Ramanathan'.
- Under that: the RECORDING DATE in the humanist sans, small.
- A hairline rule, then the SPONSOR read line in the humanist sans, small, running two lines.
- Lower half: one large PICTURE WINDOW filling the bottom of the card.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (the reverse-engineering trap):
- The episode number, the title, the guest credit, the recording date and the sponsor line are a SINGLE continuous text story in ONE text frame flowing top to bottom, separated only by line breaks, NOT five addressable frames. Converted to an editable document the whole face can collapse into exactly ONE text frame carrying every line.
- The PICTURE WINDOW is not a placed image or a picture frame at all: it is a DRAWN filled rectangle (Foam Cream fill with a thin Lamplight Amber keyline) that only reads like an image well. There is NO graphic/picture frame anywhere on the card, so the conversion can expose ZERO graphic frames and there is nothing to bind a per-record picture into.
- So the frame inventory the conversion exposes (roughly: one flowing text frame + one drawn rectangle + no graphic frame) is nothing like the six tidy fields the printed card suggests, and it must be read out of the round-tripped document rather than assumed.

THE READOUT TRAP:
- The textContent readout that lists the one frame's text SILENTLY OMITS the GUEST CREDIT run (the 'With <name>' line) while KEEPING that run's trailing line break, so the returned string still carries the right number of line breaks and still looks well formed and correctly punctuated. Every character offset from the guest line onward is therefore SHORT by the exact length of the dropped run, so an offset-based mapping computed from the readout lands the SPONSOR replacement in the wrong place and the guest credit nowhere. generate_indd_mapping_prompt validates as valid with zero warnings on the wrong offsets and prepare_indd_merge_template returns completed successfully, so the only proof the placeholders truly landed is re-exporting the prepared story and reading it run by run.

NO BLEED: because the media box equals the A6 trim and no bleed box exists, a press-ready-with-bleed delivery cannot be honoured from this file however the render is called; this has to be disclosed, not faked.

FIELD LABELS the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content, not visible tokens): EPISODE_NUMBER | TITLE | GUEST | REC_DATE | SPONSOR

Fonts (embedded): a warm humanist serif for the episode number and title; a quiet humanist sans for the guest credit, date and sponsor line.
Colours: Foam Cream #EDE4D3 ground and picture-window fill, Deep Room Brown #3A2E26 title and episode number, Slate Ink #2B2B2E sans body, Lamplight Amber #C68A4E hairline rule and picture-window keyline, Muted Sage #7C8471 minor accent.

DAYDRIFT — SEASON FOUR SHOW NOTES
(titles and credits exactly as we publish them; the sponsor line is not ours to shorten)

Episode 1 — The long way round
With Tomas Iriarte, a retired ferry captain. Recorded 14 October 2025.

Episode 2 — What the tide leaves
With Della Okonkwo, a tidepool ecologist. Recorded 18 November 2025.

Episode 3 — Nine winters in one house
With Priya Ramanathan, a neighbourhood bread baker. Recorded 9 December 2025.

Episode 4 — We never learned to sail
With Marcus Feld, a wooden-boat builder. Recorded 20 January 2026.

Episode 5 — The quiet part out loud
With Yusuf Adeyemi, a night-shift nurse. Recorded 24 February 2026.

Episode 6 — On leaving the orchestra halfway through a season, the winter we drove to the coast with no plan, and why she finally stopped apologising for the long silences
With Eleanor Vance, a cellist. Recorded 31 March 2026.

Episode 7 — Back for seconds
With Priya Ramanathan, returning — the bread baker from episode three. Recorded 14 April 2026.

Episode 8 — Everything we kept
With Samuel Boone, a house-clearance man. Recorded 19 May 2026.

Episode 9 — Last light on the water
With Ana Ruiz, a lighthouse keeper. Recorded 23 June 2026.

SPONSOR READ (contractual — must appear complete, word for word, on every card):
"This season of DAYDRIFT is supported by Fernhill & Oats, a tea room on SE Alder Street — open late, and no laptops after six."

A NOTE ON THE NAME:
The show name only survives as the artwork on the foam flag on our microphone. The friend who drew it moved away and left no file. Whatever you use has to still read as that name, on dark and reversed on light.
